The MD:GA labels describe the carrier blend, not the composition of undiluted clove extract. The method does not specify the basis of the 1:4 ratio; it should not be read as a verified dry extract-to-carrier mass ratio.[1]

Its Table 4 gives eugenol loading efficiencies of 70.5–75.6%, with no significant formulation effect reported (p = 0.78).[1] Here, loading efficiency compares the measured eugenol concentration after drying with the theoretical concentration before drying; it is not the eugenol mass fraction of the powder.[1]

The clove paper's measure concerns surface and core phenolics; the eugenol paper compares experimental with theoretical eugenol content.
The clove paper calculates (total core phenolics − surface phenolics) / total core phenolics × 100; the eugenol paper compares experimental with theoretical eugenol content.
Neither the seven-day salt-chamber test nor the clove paper's separate sealed-tube storage experiments establish a pouch barrier requirement, a desiccant dose or a shelf life.[1]

The clove paper separately tested storage in screw-capped tubes at 4 or 25 °C for 40 days and in sealed tubes at 60 °C for seven days.[1] Neither those storage tests nor the seven-day humidity exposure establish a pouch barrier requirement, a desiccant dose or a shelf life.[1]
